newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV CLOSES DOWN 37 PCT FROM END-1996.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV CLOSES DOWN 37 PCT FROM END-1996.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev lost 37 percent in the first two trading days of 1997 for the local interbank market, closing at a new record low of 695-698 per dollar on Saturday in extremely thin volume, dealers said.

The lev opened at 620-660 per dollar and traded at 640-650 at midday, down from 590-605 at Friday's close and from 507-510 on Monday, the last trading day of 1996 for the local market before the New Year recess.
"Big final clients bid for large foreign currency volumes while banks and clients alike were reluctant to sell amid an ongoing lev slide," a commercial bank dealer said.
"Final clients bought every dollar offered irrespective of the high price," another dealer said.
The central bank was not seen selling dollars to support the crumbling lev, traders said. Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Markets were closed in Bulgaria from Tuesday through Thursday for the New Year.

Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Sunday that BNB powers to counter pressure on the lev through interventions were limited because payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt in 1997 would be a priority for the BNB.

Low BNB foreign exchange reserves, lack of financing from abroad and lower than expected privatisation proceeds in 1996 were the reasons why the central bank could not prevent the lev decline, Filipov said.
BNB forex reserves stood at $525 million at the end of November last year, down from $1.408 billion a year earlier.
Bulgaria has to meet some $300 million of foreign debt payments in the first quarter with $170-180 million due in January alone. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
